title: One Word, Two Jobs
objectives: I can tell that one word can have more than one meaning.
I can use the words around a word to choose the right meaning.
I can use ten words in two different ways.
I can write two sentences that show two meanings of the same word.
rationale: Third graders meet many words that look the same but mean different things, and the page does not say which meaning to use. This unit teaches ten common multiple-meaning words, chosen because both meanings appear in grade 3-4 reading and math. The word record's main definition is the first meaning; the other meanings are listed under senses. The cloze practice deliberately uses the first meaning in one sentence and another meaning in the second, so students must read the clues around the blank. The routine is the same for all ten: find the clue words, name the meaning, and test it in the sentence.

passage.title: Field Trip to the Pond
paras: Each pupil in Mr. Reyes's class carried a notebook to the pond. "Today you are scientists," he said in a firm voice. "Sit still and look closely." Mia leaned against the trunk of an old willow tree and opened her notebook to a clean page.

A duck paddled by, dipping its bill into the water. Omar held up a tiny silver scale he had found on the shore. "It fell off a fish," said Mr. Reyes. "See how it shines in your palm?" Omar grinned and tried to pitch a pebble to the middle of the pond, but it landed near the edge.

Then the sky turned gray. A cold spell had been in the forecast, and the wind began to whip the branches. "Time to go!" called Mr. Reyes. The class began to charge up the hill toward the bus, holding their notebooks over their heads.
On the bus, Mia tied the string of her notebook into a bow and read her notes. She had written the names of five plants, one bird, and one fish. It had been a short trip, but she had learned a lot.

qs.q: In paragraph 3, the word "spell" most nearly means
choices: to say the letters of a word
qs.why: The sentence says a cold spell was in the forecast, so spell means a short period of weather.
The class runs up the hill toward the bus, so charge means rush forward.

qs.q: Why does Mr. Reyes say, "Time to go!"?
choices: The cold, windy weather is coming.
The bus is leaving without them.
qs.why: The sky turns gray and the wind whips the branches, so the weather is changing.

qs.q: What is a central idea of the story?
choices: Ducks can swim in cold water.
A class trip to a pond helped students notice nature.
A good scientist always carries a ribbon.
qs.why: The story is about students looking closely at a pond and learning from what they see.

teacher.overview: Students learn ten words that each have more than one meaning, read a story that uses several of them, and practice using clue words to choose the right meaning.

notes.va.trunk.n: Three meanings: tree, elephant, car. Hold up a picture for each. Say: the words around trunk tell which one.
notes.va.scale.n: Meanings: tool for weight, fish plate, musical scale. Kitchen scale in the classroom helps, and so does a picture of a fish.
notes.va.pitch.v: Verb meanings: throw, set up a tent. A noun meaning, how high a sound is, is also listed. Use gestures to help students tell them apart.
notes.va.charge.v: Rush forward, ask a price, fill a battery. Students know the battery meaning; build from it. Practice with three sentences and a thumbs sign for each meaning.
notes.va.pupil.n: A student, and the black center of the eye. Show a photo of an eye in bright and dim light to teach the second meaning.
notes.va.firm.adj: Hard, or strong in a decision; also a business. Compare with soft. The cloze items use the first two meanings.
notes.va.bow.n: Pronounced two ways: BOH (ribbon, bow and arrow) and BOW rhyming with cow (bend forward). Say the word aloud for each picture so the sound is attached to the meaning.
notes.va.spell.n: Magic words, to say the letters, and a short time. Students often know only one; ask them to teach their partner the other.
notes.va.palm.n: Hand part, and a tree. Ask students to point to their palm and then draw a palm tree.
notes.va.bill.n: Bird mouth part, and a paper that tells what is owed. Compare with beak. Show a restaurant bill.

teacher.model: Think-aloud: "The sentence says a cold spell was in the forecast. A spell can be magic words, but a forecast is about weather, so spell must mean a short time of weather. The clue word forecast tells me which meaning to use."
